Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the middle. Tammy Beaumont and Amy Jones will open the batting for England Women. It will be Marizanne Kapp to start things off with the first new ball. Beaumont to face. Will Kapp get any swing under the lights? Let's see. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

6 overs? 10 overs? How many overs will this run chase last? While we get ready for the second innings to start, we take a look at scores elsewhere. Australia have retained the Chappell-Hadlee Trophy as Mitchell Marsh continues his wonderful run as T20I skipper. This is his 8th bilateral series as captain and he has won the previous 6, with one ending in a tie. The second T20I ending as a no result has kept his record clean with the third T20I, scheduled to be played on Sunday, 4th October, will only be to check whether it will be his 7th series win or stay as 6. In Ahmedabad, India have finished Day 2 strongly on 448/5, extending their lead over West Indies to a mammoth 286. After a hundred from KL Rahul, Dhruv Jurel and Ravindra Jadeja joined the party with tons each, adding a fine 206 for the 5th wicket. India were in a bit of bother at 218/4 when Rahul fell but the Jurel-Jadeja stand has probably batted the Windies out of this Test. Who knows, if India get bowled out by Lunch on Saturday or even declare, this Test might not even see a Day 4.

Whom would have bet on as the finalists of this World Cup? Australia and India? Ummm.. perhaps. However, come 3rd October, many would be forced to tweak that. Forgot the team who made it to the last two consecutive finals of the ODI World Cup? Or, adding further, three in the last four? England Women. They have reminded everyone not to take them lightly, even if this tournament is being played in Asia. They have come in with three spinners and the third was barely required. A massive statement for their campaign.

Was the surface a minefield? By no means. Yes, it is a difficult pitch to bat on but definitely not a 69 all out one. England Women stuck to their basics, but South Africa Women forgot theirs, not showing enough application with their footwork. England kept the ball at the stumps and were rewarded. They seem to be in line to boost their net run rate straightaway and jump to the top of the table, above Australia. Having said that, there is one person who will not throw in the towel. She would want to make 69 worth 200 and make England stretch themselves to chase this down. Marizanne Kapp. ​​​​Can South Africa Women pick up a few wickets and take something out of this game? The run chase will begin in a short while.

England Women's LAUREN BELL is in for a chat. She says that Linsey Smith had set the tone for them, and the rest of the bowlers showed up, doing their job as well. Adds that Linsey is a skillful bowler and does well with the new ball. Further says that the pitch looked skiddy, and they have done a good job of restricting South Africa Women to a low total. Ends by saying that it was a dream start for them and they couldn't be happier.

The previous paragraph counts for England Women as well. Excellent captaincy from Nat Sciver-Brunt. She used a seamer early on and found that Lauren Bell was struggling a bit. But from the other end, spin was getting purchase and she kept spin going on from that end, till the 20th over. And then, once the balls went a bit softer, she got on spin from both ends. Linsey Smith was her trump card, as she swung and drifted the ball when it was new, picking up 3 wickets in 19 balls, ending with bowling figures of 4-2-7-3. After that, Sophie Ecclestone came on and got turn, which further compounded South Africa Women's batters' problems. She finished with 2 scalps while the skipper helped herself to 2 wickets as well. In the end, everyone bowled as a unit and got at least a wicket.

You can have a powerful batting lineup. You can possess a quality bowling attack. But you need to assess the conditions first, which South Africa Women simply did not. They struggled to adapt to the pitch, which looked a bit sticky and played their shots way too early. Neither could they adjust to the swing, which was marginal, nor the spin, which was also marginal. That seemed to suggest that they were unsure about their footwork and ended up folding cheaply. By the 6th over, they were 4 down and the rest just folded up, with only Sinalo Jafta showing some intent, making 22.

124 balls. That's all the first innings has lasted. 69 runs scored, with one batter reaching double digits and the second highest score coming from the extras. It has been nothing short of a nightmarish start for South Africa Women, as they get bundled out for their THIRD LOWEST ODI total and second lowest in World Cups, in a completed innings. They came into this contest with full of confidence and anticipation but have just been blown away in a span of under 90 minutes.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Well, England Women need some cold drinks but do South Africa Women need some hot drinks? A terrifying set of 15 overs, if you are a Saffa fan. And a magnificent one, if you are an English one. If you are neutral. you are perhaps already thinking of the clash between Afghanistan and Bangladesh at 2.30 pm GMT later tonight. Because, it has been nothing short of disappointing from the Women In Green. They have been unsure of their footwork, not committing fully forward and not coming to terms with the pitch. There has been swing, drift and a bit of turn, with some balls stopping on the pitch. It is like trouble coming in all patterns at them and they have failed against every pattern. When just one batter has reached double digits, it tells you the story. Not much batting left and it will all be about playing for pride now, to try and play as many overs as possible, try and get past 100 and maybe, get to 140-150. Not sure whether that would be enough, but at least, it will be some fight shown. England Women, barring Lauren Bell, have hit their mark right from ball one, with the spinners making merry, claimg 4 out of the 7 wickets to fall. They will aim to wrap this innings up before the 25th over.

OUT! BOWLED! That has gone right through and Smith has two wickets in 7 balls, without conceding a single run! Tazmin Brits expects the ball to maybe just come in with the angle and comes half forward to defend. However, this one swings in through the air, lands and then goes right between bat and pad, to hit the leg stump! That's simply a marvellous ball and wonderful skill to have - swing the new ball and spjn when it gets older. Brits' run of three successive ODI tons comes to an end, as she departs for 5 (7) this time. South Africa Women are 12/2 after 3.1 overs!

Commentary.Commentary: The anthems have been sung and the players disperse. The English get together for a compulsory huddle. We mean, that's what we see in every game these days. Despite having their plans laid out in the dressing room, the players still like to have one last meeting before taking on the field. Could be like how we used to feel about last day revision before going for the exam, aye? Right. The huddle is done and the English spread out to the middle. The openers for South Africa Women, skipper Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits, have a discussion with each other before taking the field. It will be the smiling Lauren Bell to kick things off, to the Protea skipper. Irrespective of the situation, Bell always manages a smile. Great asset. Here we go then!
The squads of both sides are out in the middle, for the national anthems. It will be South Africa's anthem first, followed by that of England's.

PITCH REPORT - Former New Zealand cricketer, KATEY MARTIN, has the first look at the pitch. She starts with the conditions, calling them very sticky, hot and humid. Adds that the dimensions read 67 metres down the ground from one side, but one side square is just 53 metres long. Former West Indian star, CARLOS BRATHWAITE, now comes forward to inspect the deck. Feels that there seems to be some live grass with some cracks either side of the pitch. Believes that moisture on the surface due to the covers will overpower the cracks and spin will play a big part as was seen during the World Cup opener between India Women and Sri Lanka Women.

The skipper of South Africa Women, LAURA WOLVAARDT, says that the pitch looks a bit slower and they will look to put up a good score. She says that they are focusing on one game at a time. She adds that the new head coach is amazing and he is giving a lot of motivational talks as well. Ends by saying that they have a balanced side today with 4 seam options and 3 spin options.

The skipper of England Women, NAT SCIVER-BRUNT, says that as a team, England like to go out there and make a mark on the game. Hence the decision to field. Hopes that the pitch will get better under the lights. On the team combination, Sciver-Brunt says that England have got 2 spinners and 2 seamers. Adds that there are a couple of allrounders as well in the side. On the team playing under a new combination and method post the Heather-Knight captaincy era, Nat says that the unit is quietly confident in the way it wants to go about things, especially with the bat. Details that the policy is looking to attack but also build partnerships. With the ball, NSB says that the main aim is to keep picking up wickets. On Heather Knight playing her 150th ODI, Nat Sciver-Brunt says that Knight has plenty of experience. Calls it a great achievement for any side to have a player like Knight. Also, given the injuries she has had, Sciver-Brunt adds, it is great to have hare back in the side, citing that Heather's experience would be wonderful for the side.

England Women (Playing XI) - Tammy Beaumont, Amy Jones (WK), Heather Knight, Nat Sciver-Brunt (C), Sophia Dunkley, Emma Lamb, Alice Capsey, Charlie Dean, Sophie Ecclestone, Linsey Smith and Lauren Bell.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Sune Luus, Marizanne Kapp, Anneke Bosch, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Chloe Tryon, Nadine De Klerk, Ayabonga Khaka, Masabata Klaas and Nonkululeko Mlaba.
TOSS - England Women have won the toss and will BOWL first.

While the forecast is for a stop-start day due to the inclement weather that has already affected preparations, all eyes will be on the players to deliver high-quality cricket when they can. Get ready for a thrilling display of women's cricket as England Women take on South Africa Women! Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Across the turf, South Africa are riding on their own wave of strong recent form, led by the composed Laura Wolvaardt. Having agonizingly come close to an ICC trophy in recent years, the Proteas Women will be hungry for success. The explosive batting of Tazmin Brits and the all-round brilliance of Marizanne Kapp provide a solid core for a side that possesses great balance and depth, ready to challenge England's historical dominance over them in this format.

England Women arrive with confidence under their new captain Nat Sciver-Brunt, boosted by excellent warm-up victories Over India Women and the mighty Aussies. Their squad is a powerhouse of talent, boasting game-changing batters like Tammy Beaumont and Sophia Dunkley, complemented by a world-class spin attack featuring Sophie Ecclestone and Charlie Dean, bowlers who will relish the spin-friendly conditions expected across the venues. With Sciver-Brunt also back to bowling, their all-round threat is undeniable.

Welcome to the fourth fixture of the ICC Women's World Cup, a marquee clash set to light up the Barsapara Stadium in Guwahati! Two of the strongest contenders for this year’s title, England Women and South Africa Women, are set to commence their campaigns in what promises to be an enthralling encounter. This battle for early supremacy is crucial, as both sides look to gain vital momentum in a tournament where every group stage victory will count towards a semi-final berth.
... MATCH DAY ...

The 2025 ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup rolls on to Match 4, where England will take on South Africa at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati. Two of the tournament’s contenders will be eager to kick off their campaigns on a winning note. England come into this World Cup keen to make amends after falling short in the previous edition's final against Australia and bowing out in the group stage of the 2024 T20 World Cup. Nat Sciver-Brunt has taken over the captaincy from Heather Knight post the Ashes debacle, and as one of the game’s premier all-rounders, she will be central to her side’s hopes with both bat and ball. Encouragingly, England registered two confidence-boosting warm-up wins against India and Australia. Their batting, long reliant on Sciver-Brunt, is strengthened by Knight’s return, whose experience against spin could prove vital in subcontinental conditions. Amy Jones and Tammy Beaumont provide solidity at the top, while the middle order boasts plenty of options. Alice Capsey, fresh off a century against Australia, adds depth and a useful off-spin option. Sophia Dunkley and Emma Lamb were also among the runs in warm-ups, and Danni Wyatt-Hodge brings valuable experience of playing in India. England’s bowling will lean heavily on spin to control proceedings. Sophie Ecclestone, Sarah Glenn, Charlie Dean, and Linsey Smith form a potent spin unit, with Ecclestone and Dean also contributing with the bat. The pace attack is relatively inexperienced after Kate Cross’s omission, but Lauren Bell leads the line confidently following a strong domestic season, supported by Lauren Filer and Em Arlott. With this balance, England look well-equipped to challenge for their fifth ODI crown. On the other hand, South Africa have experienced highs and near misses in recent World Cups, exiting in the semifinals of the past two ODI editions and falling short at the final hurdle in T20 World Cups in 2023 and 2024. The Proteas Women will be eager to go all the way this time around. South Africa have been in action in the lead-up, with a triumphant ODI series in Pakistan and a win in warm-up games against Pakistan in Colombo, while another game was washed out. Led by Laura Wolvaardt, adept against spin, the captain will spearhead the batting effort. Her opening partner, Tazmin Brits, has done much of the heavy lifting this year in ODIs. Sune Luus and Marizanne Kapp complete the nucleus of the batting unit, and the performance of this quartet will go a long way in shaping the team’s fortunes. The all-round department features Nadine De Klerk and Chloe Tryon, with Anneke Bosch and Annerie Dercksen providing further depth. Much of the spin responsibility rests on Nonkululeko Mlaba, supported by Tryon and Nondumiso Shangase. The pace attack will be led by Kapp, with Ayabonga Khaka, Masabata Klaas, and Tumi Sekhukhune forming a varied bowling unit. With a blend of experience and youth, the Proteas Women will be keen to turn near misses into a historic World Cup run. Guwahati played host to the World Cup opener between India and Sri Lanka on what turned out to be a good cricket wicket, which had something in it for everyone. Let’s hope we are treated to another entertaining contest. Who are you backing to come out on top in this clash?
